title: pkix-chain-simple::Error wraps pkix_path::Error directly in public surface
description:
pkix_chain_simple::Error::Path(PathError) wraps pkix_path::Error directly without an opaque boundary. This locks pkix-chain-simple's major version to pkix-path's major version. The From<PathError> impl at line 386 and the Error::Path variant expose the upstream type directly.

The sibling pkix-chain crate makes the same choice (Error::Path(pkix_path::Error)), so this is a workspace-wide pattern rather than an isolated case. However, pkix-chain is documented as a high-level umbrella that intentionally re-exports pkix-path types, while pkix-chain-simple is documented as the 'strict, opinionated' simplified alternative — it has more reason to present a fully-opaque error surface since its callers are explicitly not looking for pkix-path-level granularity.

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: A major version bump in pkix-path forces a major version bump in pkix-chain-simple even though the simplified API's contract ('pass/fail with diagnostic') does not need the upstream error's structure. Pre-1.0 this is free, but post-1.0 this creates unnecessary cascade.

Location: /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-chain-simple/src/lib.rs line 329 (Error::Path variant) and line 385 (From impl)
